newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai cabinet endorses property rescue package.
newsitem.headline: Thai cabinet endorses property rescue package.

text.p: The Thai cabinet on Tuesday endorsed a 70 billion baht ($2.8 billion) property sector rescue package recently proposed by Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan to help pull the industry out of a three-year slump.

Deputy Finance Minister Chavarat Chanvirakul told reporters the package included a plan for the state-owned Government Savings Bank and the Government Housing Bank to lend up to 20 billion baht of concessional mortgage loans to civil servants buying their first homes.
Chavarat did not give many more details than already announced by Amnuay last week.
Under the scheme, borrowing civil servants will be charged an eight to nine percent mortgage rate against 13-14 percent carried by normal commercial bank loans.
Another 50 billion baht contributed by the government and commercial banks would be used for temporary takeovers of private property projects facing short-term financing problems.
Central bank officials have said a special corporate entity set up for the rescue would likely buy cash-strapped but commercially viable projects at a discount to their market values.
Chavarat said the finance ministry needed to study proposals that borrowing civil servants also be offered land transfer tax exemption and other privileges.
The stock market has fallen over the past few days, which brokers and analysts attributed to a lack of details over how the rescue plan would be implemented.
The market was down 2.14 percent, or 17.60 points, at 805.29 at the lunch break on Tuesday.
